answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using graph-based trust propagation. Nodes compute reputation scores through a diffusion kernel anchored to a basalt core of vetted seeds. An adversary must obtain authentic endorsements signed by an established node's cryptographic quill, incurring a scarce cost of genuine social capital and time per identity. However, this mechanism creates severe cold-start friction, penalizing legitimate newcomers who lack prior network relationships.
